text: Hi, how's it going? I'm a big coffee lover, so I guess I'll start there. I can't really start my day without a cup of coffee, and this morning was no different. I had one before I came to take this test, and I'm already looking forward to another one once it's over. I work in IT, and my days are pretty busy. I live in an apartment, and I'm pretty much a homebody. In my free time, I like listening to music, playing computer games, and reading. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell: coffee, music, and my computer. I'm happy to be here, and I hope I do well today!

Well, I make a lot of appointments, but they're mostly work meetings and doctor visits. At work, my calendar is packed, so I book meetings through my company's calendar app. For things like haircuts or the dentist, I just book online, because I hate talking on the phone. And with friends, I send a quick text, like "You free on Saturday?" Honestly, the thing is, I have a terrible memory. So my family and I share one calendar on our phones. If it's not on the calendar, it doesn't exist! I get a reminder an hour before, and that's saved me more than once. It's simple, but it works for me.

Oh, I remember this one really well. When I was about seven, I had an appointment to get a flu shot at the neighborhood clinic. I was scared to death of needles. My mom was busy, so my aunt took me. On the way there, I kept saying, "I feel fine! I don't need it!" She just laughed and held my hand tight. In the waiting room, I saw a kid crying, and that made it even worse. When it was my turn, I closed my eyes and squeezed my aunt's hand as hard as I could. And guess what? It was over in two seconds! The doctor gave me a sticker, and my aunt bought me an ice cream on the way home. To make a long story short, it wasn't scary at all, and I felt kind of silly afterward.

Let me think. Oh, yeah, there's one I can't forget. A few years ago, I had a big presentation for the executives, so I booked a haircut the day before to look sharp. My usual barber was out that day, so a young guy I'd never met took over. I was so tired that I fell asleep in the chair. When I woke up, I looked in the mirror, and it was a total mess! He'd given me an almost-buzz cut! I couldn't help but laugh, but inside I was panicking. The next day, I walked into the meeting like nothing was wrong. The funny thing is, my boss said, "You look so fresh today!" It turned out to be a good-luck haircut, because the presentation went great. Since then, I never fall asleep in a barber's chair.

I'd like to talk about my best friend. We met in college and we've been close for over twenty years. He lives in Busan now, so we don't see each other a lot, but we talk almost every week. The first thing you notice about him is that he's super funny. He can make anybody laugh, even at a boring meeting! He's also a really loyal friend. When I had a rough time at work, he drove all the way to my city just to buy me dinner. He doesn't say much about feelings, but he's always there when you need him. Honestly, he's like family to me. I'm lucky to have a friend like him.

With my family, we're really into game nights. Every Friday, after dinner, we turn on the TV and play Mario Kart together. Everybody plays. I'm a gamer, so I thought I'd win easily. But, to be honest, the youngest player destroys me every time! He's so fast, and he knows all the shortcuts. I always end up in last place, and everyone laughs so hard. Sometimes I get so serious that I shout at the screen. Somebody always rolls their eyes. It's pretty silly, but it's the one time of the week when everyone puts their phones down. I love that. Nothing beats a night of games and snacks with the family.

The last time was about a month ago, when my best friend came down from Busan. He called me out of the blue and said, "Let's go fishing!" So early Saturday morning, we went to a small dock near my place. We bought a cup of coffee on the way, of course. We sat there for about four hours, and honestly, we didn't catch a single fish! Not one! He kept saying, "The fish must be on vacation." We were laughing the whole time. In the end, we gave up, and went to a raw fish restaurant for lunch. We ate way too much, and he paid. So we didn't catch anything, but it was still a great day. We talked about old college days, and I felt like a kid again.

The park I like the most is a lake park on a hill, just behind my apartment. It's only a ten-minute walk, which is really convenient. There's a small lake in the middle, and a walking trail goes all the way around it. It's surrounded by tall pine trees, so it's really peaceful. On weekends, it's pretty lively. You'll see older people doing stretching exercises, kids riding bikes, and couples taking photos by the water. Some people bring a mat and have a picnic. There's also a little cafe, where I always grab a coffee, and I sit on a bench and watch the ducks. To me, it's the best way to clear my head.

To be honest, I wasn't a park person at all. I started going about five years ago, when work got really stressful. I was in front of my computer all day long, and I was totally burned out. One day, a coworker said to me, "Come on, let's take a walk at lunch." I said, "Nah, I'm too busy." But he dragged me out anyway. We walked around the lake park for twenty minutes, and I couldn't believe how good I felt. The fresh air was amazing, and my head felt so clear. After that, I started going every day. Now I think it's the best habit I've ever picked up.

One time, I took my friend's kid to fly a kite at the park. It was a windy autumn Saturday, perfect for it. I told him, "I'm a pro at this!" Well, that was a big mistake. The kite flew up really high, and then the string snapped! The kite went flying toward the lake, and the kid screamed, "Go get it!" So I ran after it like a crazy person. The kite landed in a muddy field next to the lake. I jumped in to grab it, and my shoe got stuck in the mud! I pulled my foot out, but the shoe stayed behind! I was standing there in one sock, holding a muddy kite. The kid was laughing so hard that he fell on the grass. Other people were watching and laughing too. I was so embarrassed, but I couldn't stop laughing either. It's one of those moments we still talk about at dinner.

Hi, I'm calling to get some help planning a trip. My friend and I are thinking about going to Bangkok for five days in the spring. We'd like to eat a lot of street food, visit some temples, and just relax. I have a few questions. First, do you have any package deals for two people?. Okay. Does the package include flights and a hotel, or do I need to book them separately?. Got it. What's the best time of year to go? I heard it gets really hot.. Also, do Korean citizens need a visa?. One last thing: how much would it cost in total for two people?. That sounds good. Could you send me the details by email? Thanks a lot for your help!

Hi, it's me again. I'm afraid I have a problem. I bought a non-refundable ticket to Bangkok last week, but something came up at work. We have a big system project, and I can't leave. I know the ticket is non-refundable, but I was hoping we could work something out. First, could I change the date to a later time, even if I pay a change fee? If that's not possible, could I get a travel credit that I can use later this year? And if neither works, can I transfer the ticket to someone else, like a coworker? I really want to avoid wasting the money. Which of these do you think is the best option? I'd really appreciate your help.

Yes, and it was a total disaster! Two years ago, my friends and I wanted to go to Jeju in October. I thought, "There's plenty of time," so I put it off. Big mistake. When I finally tried to book, all the flights were sold out! Every single one! It was a holiday week, and the hotels were full too. My friend looked at me like, "You're the IT guy, and you couldn't book a flight?" I didn't give up. I searched for hours that night, and I found a ferry from Mokpo. It took four hours, but my friends thought it was an adventure. And I found a tiny guesthouse run by an old lady. She cooked us a homemade breakfast every morning. To be honest, it ended up being better than a fancy hotel. Lesson learned: book early!

There are so many new gadgets these days, but the one that changed my life is the robot vacuum. I bought one about three years ago, and I was kind of skeptical at first. I thought, "Can a little machine really clean my floor?" But it turned out to be amazing. I set it to run when I leave for work, and when I get home, the floor is spotless. I used to spend an hour cleaning every weekend, and now I get that time back. I even named it "Roomi"! My friends like to watch it go around the house. Also, we have an air fryer, a smart speaker, and a steam closet. All of these save time, so I have more time for the things I like. Honestly, I can't imagine life without them.

One appliance that everyone loves these days is the air fryer. It's basically a small oven that cooks food with hot air. You can make fried chicken, french fries, or even sweet potatoes without any oil. I'll admit, I was a little doubtful at first. But I tried frozen dumplings in it, and they came out crispy and delicious. Most people say it's healthier, and it's so easy to clean. I use it almost every day. Some people complain that it's a bit small, or that it's noisy. But overall, people seem really happy with it. In Korea, it's become a must-have in the kitchen. I'd say it's one of the best things we've bought.
